title: Sudden Drop in Water Pressure? Here Is What to Check
description: Experiencing weak water flow throughout your home usually stems from a few key components. First, check your main water shut-off valve to ensure it is completely open; even a partially closed valve can severely restrict household flow. Next, inspect your Pressure Reducing Valve (PRV), typically located near where the main water line enters the house. Internal PRV diaphragms can fail or become clogged over time, causing whole-house pressure to drop below normal operating levels. If low pressure is isolated to a single fixture, a clogged aerator or localized scale buildup is likely responsible. For persistent low pressure, consult a licensed plumber to test your PRV and main supply line safely.
